sources.design: SR, 26 reports, n 1912, search December 2023; no meta-analysis; very-low GRADE.
sources.population: Isolated nonoperative MCL grades I–III; not combined ACLR/multiligament rehab.
sources.comparator: Various exercise, bracing, immobilization, surgery comparisons.
sources.outcomes: Grade I/II studies often allow tolerated weight-bearing/ambulation. Exercise success 70–98%, RTS 3–12 weeks across heterogeneous reports, not a personalized prognosis. No superior protocol or universal brace timing established.
sources.uncertainty: Poor dose reporting, bias, indirectness, heterogeneity. Grade III restrictions varied; do not treat observed timelines as clearance.
sources.harms: Immobilization studies report quadriceps atrophy; no pooled exercise-harm estimate.
sources.limitations: Poor dose reporting, bias, indirectness, heterogeneity. Grade III restrictions varied; do not treat observed timelines as clearance.

protocol.progression: Grading, stability, pain/function; no validated shared algorithm.
protocol.stoppingRules: No universal numeric stop criterion; valgus-protection/bracing decisions depend on clinical assessment.

sources.design: Prospective cohort of 35 athletes; no randomized comparator.
sources.population: Athletes with isolated grade III MCL sprains; combined ligament injuries outside scope.
sources.comparator: No concurrent control; historical surgery/immobilization comparisons.
sources.coInterventions: Lateral hinged brace provides valgus support while allowing flexion/extension; pool or whirlpool ROM.
sources.outcomes: Abstract describes ROM, then quadriceps sets/leg raises; resistance added after 90-degree flexion. Mean HSS 45.9/50 (range 41–50). Historical comparisons cannot establish superiority.
sources.uncertainty: Old uncontrolled athletic cohort; full text not retrieved; dose/frequency and validated return criteria inaccessible.
sources.harms: Exercise-specific harms not reported in abstract.
sources.limitations: Old uncontrolled athletic cohort; full text not retrieved; dose/frequency and validated return criteria inaccessible.

protocol.execution: reported in accessible text: Abstract describes lateral hinged valgus-support bracing allowing knee motion, initial pool/whirlpool ROM, then quadriceps setting and leg raises. Exact exercise setup and brace use during each exercise remain unspecified.
protocol.dose: not reported as repetitions, holds, resistance or program duration in the inspected abstract; mean 5.3 years is follow-up, not intervention duration.
protocol.frequency: not reported in the inspected abstract; full methods not retrieved.
protocol.supervision: not reported as a session-supervision schedule in the inspected abstract; full methods not retrieved.
protocol.progression: reported in accessible text: Abstract adds resistive exercise when 90 degrees of knee flexion is present and allows unrestricted sports upon recovery. This describes the selected 35-athlete isolated grade III program; recovery criteria and loading details remain unspecified, not universal clearance.
protocol.stoppingRules: not reported as an exercise stopping rule in the inspected abstract; return upon recovery lacks precise clearance criteria.

sources.population: Isolated grade III MCL; stress radiographs 6–10 mm medial opening; arthroscopy excluded cruciate, meniscus and cartilage injury.
sources.outcomes: All good/excellent; 60% had minimal 3-mm residual laxity. No significant modality difference except faster work return with mobilization. Effect CI not given.

sources.harms: Residual laxity in 60%; other harms not reported.
sources.limitations: Very small old trial; abstract only; does not demonstrate unrestricted valgus/pivoting safety.

exerciseMappings.matchRationale: No equivalence to a dynamic catalog leg extension or genericduration progression. Abstract establishes exercise name but does not support an executable dose; full protocol required before commissioned PNG.
Do not equate unspecified clinical legraise to abdominal straight-legraise or other hip exercise. Preserve exact known/unknown details and seek primary protocol; no artwork provenance fabricated.

proposedRules.statement: Candidate ordinary-workout gate: withhold automatic injured-knee loading/progression when MCL grade, stability, associated injury or clinician restrictions are unknown. Obtain an individual plan rather than inventing a brace duration, valgus-load ceiling or return date.

applicability.population: Clinically graded isolated MCL sprain; grades I–III assessed distinctly.
applicability.stage: Acute healing and residual instability; grade and injury location matter.
applicability.rationale: Sparse grade-specific protocols and studies of assessed isolated injury cannot support an unknown-stage automated routine.

proposedRules.limitations: Product precaution rather than a published permanent contraindication; clinical review needed. No universal prohibition of motion or strength implied.

proposedRules.statement: Retain early quadriceps-setting and leg-raise names as protocol-retrieval candidates only. Full clinical execution and grade/stage-specific dosage must be resolved before app use.

applicability.population: Clinician-managed isolated MCL sprains resembling the athlete cohort.
applicability.stage: Early braced functional rehabilitation under clinical assessment.
applicability.rationale: Primary abstract identifies exercises but supplies insufficient executable detail.

proposedRules.limitations: Historical uncontrolled cohort; not demonstrated superior to other management; no unsupervised protocol released.
